items.stem: Define the term "cultural tourism".
items.answer: Travel to experience the heritage, arts and way of life of a place
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: travel to experience the heritage, arts and way of life of a place. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Explain why the Butler model is useful for tourism planners.
items.answer: It suggests that destinations change over time and may stagnate or decline if they become overcrowded or lose appeal, so planners can act early to rejuvenate or manage growth.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: It suggests that destinations change over time and may stagnate or decline if they become overcrowded or lose appeal, so planners can act early to rejuvenate or manage growth. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Ingrid writes: "Ecotourism always has no environmental impact." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Even ecotourism involves flights and visitors in fragile areas; it must be carefully managed and limited.
items.markingKey: Even ecotourism involves flights and visitors in fragile areas; it must be carefully managed and limited. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Using Benidorm, Spain as an example, explain the Butler model.
items.answer: A fishing village in the 1950s, it became one of Europe's first mass-tourism resorts with high-rise hotels; it has since tried to rejuvenate its image. It moved from exploration to development and consolidation, then had to rejuvenate to avoid decline.
items.markingKey: Context (A fishing village in the 1950s, it became one of Europe's first mass-tourism resorts with high-rise hotels; it has since tried to rejuvenate its image.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: it moved from exploration to development and consolidation, then had to rejuvenate to avoid decline. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to the Butler model.

items.stem: Evaluate the research question "Why do people go on holiday?" for an MYP Individuals and Societies investigation into the growth of global tourism: causes and types of tourism. Rewrite it so that it is clear, focused and researchable.
items.answer: Weakness: it is a general question without a place or period to investigate Improved: "How has the type of tourist visiting Bali changed between 1990 and 2024?"
items.markingKey: 1 mark: weakness identified (it is a general question without a place or period to investigate); 1-2 marks: a focused question such as "How has the type of tourist visiting Bali changed between 1990 and 2024?" (clear scope – place, period or group – and open, researchable wording); 1 mark: justification of the change. Criterion B (investigating): a clear, focused research question whose relevance is justified, a realistic action plan, appropriate and varied methods/sources, and reflection on the process.

items.stem: Formulate an action plan to investigate the research question "How has the type of tourist visiting Bali changed between 1990 and 2024?" Include the main steps, at least one primary and one secondary source, and how you would record your findings.
items.answer: Collect Indonesian statistics on arrivals by origin and purpose; read two case studies; apply the Butler model; compare decades; evaluate sources; cite in APA.
items.markingKey: Indicative plan: Collect Indonesian statistics on arrivals by origin and purpose; read two case studies; apply the Butler model; compare decades; evaluate sources; cite in APA. Credit: logical sequence of steps with a timeline; varied, appropriate sources (primary and secondary) named specifically; a method for recording and citing information (e.g. a source log in MLA/APA); a step for evaluating the process and results. items.stem: By roughly how much did international arrivals fall in 2020 because of COVID-19?
items.answer: About 70%
items.markingKey: A. Borders closed worldwide.

items.stem: Briefly explain why tourism has grown in emerging economies such as China and India.
items.answer: A fast-growing middle class has more disposable income and leisure time, governments have eased travel rules, and many people now travel abroad for the first time.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: A fast-growing middle class has more disposable income and leisure time, governments have eased travel rules, and many people now travel abroad for the first time. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Distinguish between mass tourism and ecotourism.
items.answer: Mass tourism brings large numbers of visitors to developed resorts and often has big environmental impacts; ecotourism involves small numbers in natural areas and aims to conserve the environment and benefit local people.
items.markingKey: Mass tourism brings large numbers of visitors to developed resorts and often has big environmental impacts; ecotourism involves small numbers in natural areas and aims to conserve the environment and benefit local people. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: A student claims: "The number of tourists has grown steadily every year without interruption." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Growth has been interrupted by crises such as 9/11 (2001), the 2008–09 financial crisis and especially COVID-19 in 2020.
items.markingKey: Growth has been interrupted by crises such as 9/11 (2001), the 2008–09 financial crisis and especially COVID-19 in 2020. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
Source A – UN Tourism report (paraphrased): Summary of UN Tourism (formerly UNWTO) World Tourism Barometer reports, 2020–2025

International tourist arrivals reached about 1.46 billion in 2019, the tenth consecutive year of growth. In 2020 arrivals fell by around 72% as travel restrictions spread, returning tourism to levels last seen about 30 years earlier. By 2024 arrivals had almost fully recovered to pre-pandemic levels.

Evaluate Source A as evidence about the growth of global tourism: causes and types of tourism. Consider its origin, purpose, value and limitations.
items.answer: Origin: Summary of UN Tourism (formerly UNWTO) World Tourism Barometer reports, 2020–2025. Purpose: to provide data on global tourism trends for governments and industry. Value: It is the official global source of tourism statistics, based on national data. Limitation: Data depend on national reporting and include only international arrivals, not domestic tourism.
items.markingKey: Origin: Summary of UN Tourism (formerly UNWTO) World Tourism Barometer reports, 2020–2025. Purpose: to provide data on global tourism trends for governments and industry. Value: It is the official global source of tourism statistics, based on national data. Limitation: Data depend on national reporting and include only international arrivals, not domestic tourism. Award up to [3]: origin and purpose identified and USED (not just copied), at least one value and one limitation explicitly linked to them. Reliability is judged for a purpose, not as "biased = useless". "Cheap air travel is the main reason for the growth of global tourism." Using Source A and your own knowledge, to what extent do you agree?
items.answer: Cheap flights were a major enabling factor, but rising incomes and leisure time created the demand that airlines responded to.
items.markingKey: From the source: Tourism grew strongly until 2019, collapsed in 2020 and has since recovered. Own knowledge for: budget airlines and jets made long-distance travel affordable; air arrivals dominate international tourism. Own knowledge against: rising incomes and paid holidays created demand; the internet and easier visas made travel simpler. Judgement: Cheap flights were a major enabling factor, but rising incomes and leisure time created the demand that airlines responded to. items.stem: The data show international tourist arrivals (UN Tourism): 1950: 25 million; 1970: 166 million; 1990: 435 million; 2010: 952 million; 2019: 1465 million. Calculate the average rate of change per year between 1950 and 2019, and use the data to describe whether the change is speeding up or slowing down.
items.answer: +20.9 million per year (+209 per decade); speeding up
items.markingKey: (1465 − 25) ÷ (2019 − 1950) = +20.9 million/year (M1 A1); × 10 = +209 per decade (A1). Earliest interval +7.05/yr vs latest +57/yr → speeding up (R2, data quoted).

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "overtourism"?
options: Controlling where, when and how many visitors go to a site, through quotas, fees, permits or zoning
When the number of visitors exceeds what a place can manage, harming residents' quality of life and the environment
Responsible travel to natural areas that conserves the environment, sustains the well-being of local people and involves interpretation and education
Travel to experience the heritage, arts and way of life of a place
items.answer: When the number of visitors exceeds what a place can manage, harming residents' quality of life and the environment
items.markingKey: B. "overtourism" is when the number of visitors exceeds what a place can manage, harming residents' quality of life and the environment.

items.stem: Explain why overtourism causes conflict with residents.
items.answer: Crowds, noise, rising rents (as homes become short-term rentals) and high prices make cities like Barcelona and Venice harder to live in, while residents may see few benefits.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Crowds, noise, rising rents (as homes become short-term rentals) and high prices make cities like Barcelona and Venice harder to live in, while residents may see few benefits. items.stem: Plan an extended response to the question: "The benefits of tourism outweigh its costs for host communities." To what extent do you agree? Give a thesis, two arguments with specific evidence, a counter-argument and a conclusion.
items.answer: Thesis: It depends on management: when local people own businesses and visitor numbers are controlled, benefits usually outweigh costs; unmanaged mass tourism can reverse this.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: it creates jobs, foreign exchange and funds for conservation and heritage; it can support infrastructure such as airports and roads. Counter-arguments: leakage, seasonal jobs and rising costs limit local benefits; environmental damage and overtourism harm residents. Thesis/conclusion: It depends on management: when local people own businesses and visitor numbers are controlled, benefits usually outweigh costs; unmanaged mass tourism can reverse this. Credit a thesis that answers the question, logically ordered paragraphs each with specific evidence, a counter-argument that is weighed, and a conclusion that follows. Criterion C (communicating): appropriate style and register for the purpose, a clear structure suited to the format (topic sentence, developed evidence, explanation, link back to the question), accurate subject terminology, and sources documented with a recognised convention (MLA or APA).

items.stem: The number of visitors to the Galápagos Islands was 41,000 visitors in 1990 and 330,000 visitors in 2023 (approx., Galápagos National Park). Calculate the percentage change.
items.markingKey: Percentage change = (new − old) ÷ old × 100 (M1) = (330,000 − 41,000) ÷ 41,000 × 100 = +704.9% (A1). Dividing by the new value is a common error.

items.stem: Outline one way in which Costa Rica's ecotourism shows ecotourism supporting conservation.
items.answer: With about a quarter of its land protected, Costa Rica attracts millions of nature tourists; certification (CST) rewards sustainable businesses. Protected forests became an economic asset through tourism.
items.markingKey: Context (With about a quarter of its land protected, Costa Rica attracts millions of nature tourists; certification (CST) rewards sustainable businesses.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: protected forests became an economic asset through tourism. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to ecotourism supporting conservation.

items.stem: International tourist arrivals worldwide went from 25 million in 1950 to 1,465 million in 2019. Which is the percentage change?
Write one well-structured paragraph (Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link) in answer to this question: Explain why the multiplier effect can spread the benefits of tourism.
items.answer: Tourists' spending pays hotel and restaurant workers, who spend their wages locally; businesses buy from local farmers and suppliers, so income circulates and creates further jobs.
items.markingKey: Content: Tourists' spending pays hotel and restaurant workers, who spend their wages locally; businesses buy from local farmers and suppliers, so income circulates and creates further jobs. Structure: a clear point that answers the question, specific evidence, explanation that links evidence to the point, and a closing link. items.stem: Explain why "How effective are community conservancies in the Maasai Mara at sharing tourism income with Maasai landowners?" is a suitable research question for an MYP investigation into sustainable tourism and ecotourism.
items.answer: It evaluates sustainable tourism with a focus on fairness and conservation.
items.markingKey: It evaluates sustainable tourism with a focus on fairness and conservation. items.stem: Lukas argues that "Cheap air travel is the main reason for the growth of global tourism." Ana disagrees. Explain one piece of evidence each student could use, and state which view you find more convincing and why.
items.answer: Cheap flights were a major enabling factor, but rising incomes and leisure time created the demand that airlines responded to.
items.markingKey: Lukas: budget airlines and jets made long-distance travel affordable. Ana: rising incomes and paid holidays created demand. Judgement (1-2 marks): Cheap flights were a major enabling factor, but rising incomes and leisure time created the demand that airlines responded to.

items.stem: Analyse one strength and one limitation of this view: "The benefits of tourism outweigh its costs for host communities."
items.answer: It depends on management: when local people own businesses and visitor numbers are controlled, benefits usually outweigh costs; unmanaged mass tourism can reverse this.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: it creates jobs, foreign exchange and funds for conservation and heritage; it can support infrastructure such as airports and roads. Arguments against: leakage, seasonal jobs and rising costs limit local benefits; environmental damage and overtourism harm residents. Supported judgement: It depends on management: when local people own businesses and visitor numbers are controlled, benefits usually outweigh costs; unmanaged mass tourism can reverse this.

items.stem: Write the introduction and an outline of the body paragraphs for an essay that evaluates the view that "Ecotourism is the best way to protect fragile environments."
items.answer: Thesis: Ecotourism can help protect environments if strictly managed and combined with other conservation funding, but it is not a complete solution.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: it gives economic value to conservation and funds parks; it involves and benefits local communities. Counter-arguments: flights and visitors still cause impacts and can grow into mass tourism; income depends on tourist numbers, which can collapse in crises. Thesis/conclusion: Ecotourism can help protect environments if strictly managed and combined with other conservation funding, but it is not a complete solution. Credit a thesis that answers the question, logically ordered paragraphs each with specific evidence, a counter-argument that is weighed, and a conclusion that follows. items.stem: You have three weeks to investigate "How much of the money spent by tourists in Zanzibar stays in the local economy?" Outline a step-by-step plan, the sources you would use and one way you would evaluate your process at the end.
items.answer: Find reports on tourism leakage in Zanzibar (World Bank, NGOs); interview a local tour operator by video call or email; categorise spending; calculate retained %; evaluate data limits; cite in APA.
items.markingKey: Indicative plan: Find reports on tourism leakage in Zanzibar (World Bank, NGOs); interview a local tour operator by video call or email; categorise spending; calculate retained %; evaluate data limits; cite in APA. items.stem: Which of the following best describes "dark tourism"?
options: Jobs that are available only during the tourist season
When the number of visitors exceeds what a place can manage, harming residents' quality of life and the environment
A holiday in which transport, accommodation and often meals are sold together at one price
Travel to sites associated with death or tragedy, such as battlefields or memorials
items.answer: Travel to sites associated with death or tragedy, such as battlefields or memorials
items.markingKey: D. "dark tourism" is travel to sites associated with death or tragedy, such as battlefields or memorials.

items.stem: State what is meant by the term "economic leakage".
items.answer: Tourist spending that leaves the destination, for example to foreign-owned hotels, airlines and imported goods
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: tourist spending that leaves the destination, for example to foreign-owned hotels, airlines and imported goods. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "sustainable tourism"?
options: A holiday in which transport, accommodation and often meals are sold together at one price
Tourism that takes full account of its current and future economic, social and environmental impacts, meeting the needs of visitors, industry, the environment and host communities
Richard Butler's 1980 tourist area life cycle: exploration, involvement, development, consolidation, stagnation, then decline or rejuvenation
The maximum number of visitors a place can support without unacceptable damage
items.answer: Tourism that takes full account of its current and future economic, social and environmental impacts, meeting the needs of visitors, industry, the environment and host communities
items.markingKey: B. "sustainable tourism" is tourism that takes full account of its current and future economic, social and environmental impacts, meeting the needs of visitors, industry, the environment and host communities.

items.stem: Explain the difference between domestic tourism and international tourism.
items.answer: Domestic tourism is travel within your own country; international tourism involves crossing a national border.
items.markingKey: Domestic tourism is travel within your own country; international tourism involves crossing a national border. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.answer: Tourists' spending pays hotel and restaurant workers, who spend their wages locally; businesses buy from local farmers and suppliers, so income circulates and creates further jobs.

items.stem: "Higher fees always reduce local benefits." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Fees can fund conservation and local services if revenue is shared with communities.
items.markingKey: Fees can fund conservation and local services if revenue is shared with communities. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain the difference between mass tourism and ecotourism.
items.answer: Mass tourism brings large numbers of visitors to developed resorts and often has big environmental impacts; ecotourism involves small numbers in natural areas and aims to conserve the environment and benefit local people.
items.markingKey: Mass tourism brings large numbers of visitors to developed resorts and often has big environmental impacts; ecotourism involves small numbers in natural areas and aims to conserve the environment and benefit local people. items.stem: "Tourism always brings large economic benefits to local people." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Benefits depend on who owns businesses and where supplies come from; with high leakage, local people may gain little.
items.markingKey: Benefits depend on who owns businesses and where supplies come from; with high leakage, local people may gain little. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Briefly explain why ecotourism can still harm the environment.
items.answer: Long-haul flights add to emissions, popular ecotourism areas can become crowded, and building lodges and roads in fragile areas causes damage.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Long-haul flights add to emissions, popular ecotourism areas can become crowded, and building lodges and roads in fragile areas causes damage. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

Source A – Government policy statement (paraphrased): Paraphrase of statements by the Tourism Council of Bhutan on the reopening of tourism, 2022

The government announced that the daily Sustainable Development Fee would fund projects that preserve the country's culture and environment and improve infrastructure. The aim was to attract visitors who valued the country's heritage, rather than large numbers of low-spending tourists.

Source A – Newspaper report (paraphrased): Paraphrase of international news reports on protests in Barcelona, July 2024

Thousands of residents marched through central Barcelona, some spraying tourists with water pistols, to protest against mass tourism. They argued that short-term rentals had pushed up rents and that the city's economy depended too much on visitors. The mayor announced plans to end licences for tourist apartments by 2028.
